title: Effort-to-Outcome Mapping Notebook — Claire Nguyen
content:
Purpose:
A scratchpad for translating the small, daily efforts I do into measurable outcomes for Q4->Q1. Trying to move away from activity lists (PRs merged, meetings attended) toward forecasting impact (reduced onboarding time, fewer support tickets, higher template re-use).

Context / why this matters right now:
- DevEx has a backlog of small surface-area wins that never move the needle in dashboards.
- Leadership is asking for measurable improvements we can show in Customer Health and onboarding metrics for Hosted API.
- I'm the individual contributor owner for quickstarts & templates for the next 6 weeks; need a lightweight operating model to decide what I actually do.

High-level Objective:
Reduce average new-customer time-to-first-success by 30% for the Hosted API quickstart path, measured from signup -> first successful request in prod/console, by end of Q1.

My outcome hypotheses (ranked):
1) Hypothesis: A curated "minimal quickstart" with step-by-step copy + 1-click snippet will convert 25% more trial signups to first-success within 1 day.
   - Metric (primary): % of trial signups with first-success within 24h (baseline 12%).
   - Secondary: drop-off points in the flow, time-to-first-success median/p95.
   - Measurement plan: instrument quickstart modal events (open, click snippet, run request) — link event schema in linked_artifacts.

2) Hypothesis: Adding a small troubleshooting checklist in the onboarding email will cut support tickets about "401/key issues" by 40% for new tenants.
   - Metric: counts of support tickets tagged onboarding/key-issues in first 7 days.
   - Measurement plan: coordinate with CS to add ticket tag + weekly sampling.

3) Hypothesis: A one-page 'local dev' guide with trimmed instructions and a sample Dockerfile reduces setup time for private deployments by 20% for internal POC users.
   - Metric: self-reported time in POC survey + time between "request access" -> "first private run" for internal pilots.

Effort-to-outcome mapping (working table):
- Quickstart minimal rewrite (2 days): Expected impact +13% trial->first-success in 24h (optimistic). Confidence: medium. Dependencies: design review, analytics event piggyback. Linked ticket: JIRA-DEVEX-412.
- 1-click snippet launcher (3 days): Expected impact +8-12%. Confidence: low-medium. Risk: security review for snippet execution.
- Onboarding email checklist (half-day + ops): Expected impact - reduce 401 tickets by 30% if read. Risk: open-rate; mitigate with A/B subject lines.
- Local dev Docker-guide (1.5 days): Expected impact - 10–20% faster POC. Low risk.
- Run office-hours + recording (2 hours prep + 1 hour live): Impact: qualitative, helpful for large customers. Not primary.

Weekly experiments (log):
- Week of 2024-11-11: A/B subject lines for onboarding email (A simple checklist vs. detailed step-by-step). Result: subject A open 28% vs B 21%; checklist variant had 9% click-through to quickstart. (Note: small sample n=230).
- Week of 2024-11-25: Quickstart wireframe tested with interns (5 sessions). Feedback: too many steps, unclear API key step. Action: reorder to put "create API key" first.
- Week of 2024-12-09: Prototype snippet modal built (disabled execution). Internal test: 60% of devs used snippet copy; friction points: missing language dropdown.

Decision log / what I committed to this sprint:
- Prioritize minimal quickstart rewrite and analytics instrumentation (sprint priority A).
- Defer 1-click snippet execution until security sign-off; shipping copy + UI first.
- Add minimal onboarding checklist into first email with A/B variant, monitor ticket counts.

Unresolved questions (notes-to-self):
- What is the exact event name product expects for "first_success"? Confirm with Analytics team (ping @Marco).
- Can Support add "onboarding/key-issue" tag to tickets retroactively? If not, need to instrument forms.
- If quickstart improves time-to-first-success but not product-retention, how do we measure downstream? Add 30/60-day retention cohort metric.

Retrospective notes (short):
- Wins: rapid prototyping + user testing with interns gave clear low-cost changes that reduced steps. Email checklist had higher CTR than expected.
- Misses: underestimated security review time for executable snippets — blocked an obvious path to velocity. Need checklist for security gate early.

Next actions (next two weeks):
1) Finalize minimal quickstart copy + wireframes (due 2024-11-08) — owner: Claire.
2) Create instrumentation ticket for first_success + quickstart events (JIRA-DEVEX-412) — owner: Claire, coord Analytics.
3) Ship onboarding email checklist A variant to 30% of new signups (monitor open/click and ticket counts) — owner: Hannah.
4) Draft security pre-check for any snippet execution (1 page) — owner: Claire, ask infra/security for rubric.

Micro ritual / weekly cadence (private):
- Monday 30-min planning: pick 2 items from Effort-to-outcome table.
- Wednesday 15-min sync with Marco for analytics updates.
- Friday 20-min write-up: update this notebook with quick bullets + decisions.

Personal notes (meta):
- Keep it biased toward experiments that unblock measurable downstream outcomes (not vanity metrics).
- When in doubt, prefer instrumenting and measuring a small change vs. shipping more copy.

Quick links (for myself):
- Prototype quickstart wireframe: confluence:devex/quickstart-wireframe-v2
- Analytics event schema: confluence:analytics/event-schema#first_success
- Jira epic: JIRA:DEVEX-410 (onboarding initiatives)

End of note.
